text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Namibian government will press ahead with amending the Local Authorities Act so that the next local authority elections can be held on a party list basis instead of on a ward system basis.
- Namibia's Director of Customs, Saul Kaulinge has brushed aside allegations of a multi-million-dollar textile smuggling scam allegedly involving Namibian and South African companies.

- South African Retail Chain Pick 'n Pay Holdings Ltd has reached a franchise agreement with the Namibian Olthaver & List group, which will allow the South Africans to operate in Namibia from April this year.

- A former professor of agriculture in South Africa, Dr. Kobus Laubscher has warned Namibian farmers to engage in long term planning in order to remain competitive in the face of increasing deregulation.
- Avis Holdings has announced its intention to list on the Stock Exchanges in Namibia, Botswana and Johannesburg in April this year.
